ATTENDEES:
Keisha Morgan, Tomás Rivera, Grace Okafor, Daniel Brooks, Jordan Pike, Mei Tanaka

[14:00:12] Keisha Morgan:
    Hey everyone. Quick agenda — assortment and listing-content fixes,
    the June promo calendar, inbound inventory timing, then I want the
    back half for fulfillment and customer-escalation items that are just
    for the four of us. Jordan, Mei — you've got the partner call at
    14:35, so we'll wrap the brand portion before then.

[14:00:48] Tomás Rivera:
    Inbound first: week-4 ASN volume is up 18% over forecast. The two
    Lumen & Loom cartons that missed the Apr 26 receiving window are
    checked in now, but Kestrel's restock is still split across two
    trailers. If the second trailer lands after Thursday's cutoff, the
    trail-chair SKU goes into backorder for the weekend.

[14:01:30] Daniel Brooks:
    On listings: we fixed the missing size variants on the Lumen throw
    blanket page and the duplicate images on three Kestrel SKUs. Promo
    calendar is basically locked — Memorial Day teaser starts May 20,
    home-and-garden bundle runs May 27 to June 2, and the outdoor
    refresh pushes the first full week of June.

[14:03:55] Grace Okafor:
    Care queue is normal for a Monday. No site-wide incident, just the
    usual post-weekend delivery contacts. I'll hold specifics for the
    later segment.

[14:05:20] Keisha Morgan:
    Anything blocking the open items?

[14:05:34] Tomás Rivera:
    Just the Reno cross-dock scanner outage from Monday. It was
    intermittent again this morning. I filed a ticket with the 3PL;
    nothing back yet.

[14:06:18] Keisha Morgan:
    I'll bump it with the 3PL account lead today. Good. Jordan — Lumen &
    Loom first. You're on the spring assortment additions, right?

[14:06:55] Jordan Pike:
    Yeah. The six new textile SKUs are loaded in the portal. We still
    need the lifestyle images approved for the duvet set, and I want to
    confirm the June placement before we commit the inbound split.

[14:08:10] Daniel Brooks:
    The duvet images are in review now. Placement for June is leaning
    toward the home refresh module, but I'll confirm after the calendar
    lock on Thursday.

[14:08:50] Keisha Morgan:
    Nice. Mei — Kestrel?

[14:09:12] Mei Tanaka:
    Going okay. The camp-kitchen bundle is live; we're working on the
    replacement parts listing now. Daniel said he'd review the defect-
    rate dashboard with me on Thursday.

[14:10:30] Daniel Brooks:
    Yep, Thursday at 11. We'll go through it together.

[14:11:00] Keisha Morgan:
    Good. Couple of FYIs for the group. Swiftline Parcel carrier talks
    are ongoing — I'll have more after the May 12 call. The marketplace
    all-hands moved to next Tuesday. And reminder: Q3 assortment
    nominations are due May 15; brand partners, your portal notice has
    the official dates.

[14:13:25] Tomás Rivera:
    Quick one — are we changing the free-shipping threshold before peak?
    There were rumors.

[14:13:50] Keisha Morgan:
    No decision yet. I'll know more after leadership sync on Thursday.

[14:14:40] Daniel Brooks:
    Jordan, Mei — anything you want to flag before you head off to the
    partner call?

[14:15:05] Jordan Pike:
    No, I'm good. Thanks!

[14:15:18] Mei Tanaka:
    All good here too.

[14:15:40] Keisha Morgan:
    Cool. Let's keep the open items moving — Tomás, watch the Kestrel
    trailer; Daniel, close the listing fixes. Grace, can you walk me
    through the escalation queue shape before we get into the customer
    specifics?

[14:16:30] Grace Okafor:
    Sure. This week's queue is 41 open escalations. Nineteen are late
    delivery, twelve are returns or refunds, six are subscription-box
    issues, and four are listing or price disputes. The late-delivery
    spike is mostly Swiftline lanes out of Reno and Salt Lake.

[14:18:00] Tomás Rivera:
    Reno matches what I'm seeing inbound.

[14:18:15] Daniel Brooks:
    The price disputes are mostly coupon stacking from the weekend
    banner. Not systemic.

[14:19:30] Grace Okafor:
    Cool. I'll send the queue export to the ops channel tonight. One
    more — the Apr 18 misroute retro. We agreed on three action items:
    address-validation prompts, the carrier exception webhook, and the
    help-center macro update. Tomás owns 1, I own 2, Daniel will do the
    macro. Targeting end of next week.

[14:24:50] Keisha Morgan:
    Great. Jordan, Mei — looks like we've got about ten minutes till
    you need to head out. Any blockers we haven't covered, or anything
    you want eyes on?

[14:25:20] Jordan Pike:
    I'm good. The assortment work is unblocked. I'll have the duvet
    images approved by Friday.

[14:25:45] Mei Tanaka:
    Same here. Just the Thursday defect review with Daniel.

[14:26:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Perfect. Cool. Let's wrap the brand portion. Anything else on
    assortment, listings, promos, or inbound before Jordan and Mei step
    out?

[14:27:00] Tomás Rivera:
    Nothing from me.

[14:27:10] Grace Okafor:
    All good.

[14:27:18] Daniel Brooks:
    Same.

[14:30:00] Keisha Morgan:
    Alright, we'll do five more minutes of buffer in case anything
    comes up, then break.

[14:33:40] Keisha Morgan:
    Okay. Jordan, Mei — head on over to the partner call. Thanks for
    the updates this week.

[14:35:00] Jordan Pike:
    Thanks Keisha, see y'all next cycle.

[14:35:08] Mei Tanaka:
    Bye!

[14:35:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Okay. With Jordan and Mei off, the internal items: order
    escalations, returns, subscription cancellations, merchant terms,
    and the Swiftline rate.

[14:36:10] Keisha Morgan:
    First — order escalations. Grace has the queue; Tomás has carrier
    context. I want owners and customer-facing next steps before
    tomorrow's fulfillment planning.

[14:37:00] Keisha Morgan:
    Grace — start with the late Swiftline deliveries.

[14:37:18] Grace Okafor:
    Biggest one is Linda Ferreira, order HG-4418207. Swiftline is 6 days
    late, and she wants the shipping refunded plus a goodwill credit.
    Second is Marcus Delgado, order HG-4420913, 1187 Alder Crest Rd,
    Tacoma WA — tracking shows delivered, but he says it never arrived.

[14:39:00] Tomás Rivera:
    On HG-4418207, I can close it today with the shipping refund and a
    $25 goodwill credit. On HG-4420913, I'll file the Swiftline trace
    and reship with signature rather than leave Marcus waiting.

[14:40:30] Daniel Brooks:
    The Bend item is the Kestrel trail chair, which is already tight on
    stock. If we replace from the same pool, we risk overselling the
    weekend promo.

[14:41:00] Keisha Morgan:
    Okay. Working position: close Linda Ferreira today with the credit;
    Tomás files the trace on Marcus Delgado and reships with signature.
    Grace owns the customer messages, Tomás owns Swiftline.

[14:42:20] Keisha Morgan:
    Returns — your read?

[14:42:35] Grace Okafor:
    Twelve open return or refund cases. Most are normal. One is flagged:
    Samantha Yu, order HG-4409552, third high-value return in 60 days.
    The refund is on hold. That's the return-abuse flag. I'd keep the
    hold until the write-up is done.

[14:43:40] Tomás Rivera:
    Agreed. The 6.2-pound scan is the tell.

[14:43:55] Daniel Brooks:
    +1.

[14:44:10] Keisha Morgan:
    Great. So plan: approve the clean returns, hold HG-4409552, and Grace
    sends the abuse-flag evidence to marketplace risk after this. Keep
    the customer language neutral until risk weighs in.

[14:45:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Second — subscription cancellations. Daniel pulled the reasons; I
    want to know if any are fulfillment-caused versus merchandising.

[14:46:20] Daniel Brooks:
    Three matter for tomorrow. Hannah Cole canceled the monthly pantry
    box after two shipments arrived with duplicate items; reason code
    says "repeated packing errors." Sam O'Donnell canceled because he's
    moving and the address change didn't stick before cutoff. Erin Voss
    canceled the outdoor starter box citing "quality not worth price"
    after the Kestrel utensil kit arrived scratched.

[14:47:30] Grace Okafor:
    Hannah Cole is ours — the Reno pack line reused a pick list. Sam is
    cutoff logic, not carrier. Erin Voss is product quality plus packaging;
    the utensil kit needs a better insert.

[14:47:50] Keisha Morgan:
    Earned or not, we need the fixes. Tomás, take the Reno pick-list
    issue. Daniel, put the utensil-kit insert on the Kestrel quality
    review. Grace, make sure Hannah gets a make-good before the next
    billing date.

[14:48:40] Tomás Rivera:
    Thanks. Yeah, let's talk Reno tomorrow.

[14:49:00] Keisha Morgan:
    Third — merchant terms. Daniel has the current asks.

[14:51:30] Daniel Brooks:
    [pause] Two competing sellers are pushing for referral-fee relief.
    Alder & Ash wants 12% down to 9.5% through Q3 if they keep two-day
    handling on the top forty SKUs. BrightNest is asking for a 10.5%
    category cap in kitchen storage. I'm modeling both against the June
    promo margin.

[14:51:50] Keisha Morgan:
    I know. I'm sorry it landed there. We will figure it out.

[14:52:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Final piece, and this one is not for outside this room. Keep it
    here — no forwarding, no marketplace-channel threads, no mentions
    to anyone outside the four of us — not other ops teams, not the
    brand partners, and especially not anyone who might repeat it back
    to Swiftline before the call.

[14:53:20] Keisha Morgan:
    Swiftline Parcel — our second-largest carrier, as you know — is in
    rate talks and the signal from Renee's briefing yesterday is bad.
    Their new commercial lead is pushing roughly a 9% rate increase and
    tighter fuel surcharges. Renee thinks the final number lands
    somewhere between 7 and 11 percent. That's a direct hit to our
    delivery-promise budget for the back half of the year.

[14:55:10] Keisha Morgan:
    The implication, if it lands at 9 or worse: we likely tighten free-
    shipping thresholds in Q3 and pull two delivery-promise upgrades from
    the roadmap. That's two of the four service improvements we were
    going to launch — gone. And depending on how severe the increase is,
    there's a non-zero chance it touches weekend delivery coverage,
    though Renee is trying to avoid that and the contingency plan is to
    absorb it through thresholds first.

[14:57:00] Tomás Rivera:
    Jesus.

[14:57:15] Grace Okafor:
    Is this — is there any room to push back on the Swiftline side?

[14:57:35] Keisha Morgan:
    Vendor Relations is trying. The carrier call is May 12. If it goes
    badly we'll know within the week after. I wanted you three to know
    because (a) you're going to feel the promise and escalation impact
    directly and (b) I want you to hear about any service rollback from
    me directly, not through rumor. But I cannot stress enough — this
    stays in this room. If this leaks before leadership is ready it
    will be very bad — for the company, for me, and frankly for whoever
    leaks it.

[14:59:20] Tomás Rivera:
    Understood.

[14:59:30] Grace Okafor:
    Understood.

[14:59:35] Daniel Brooks:
    Yeah.

[15:00:10] Keisha Morgan:
    Thank you. I'll keep you updated as the Swiftline call gets closer.
    Now — let's spend the last stretch on fulfillment planning at the
    workstream level. I want to know what each of you thinks we should
    prioritize if the carrier picture turns out okay, and what we cut
    first if it doesn't.

[15:00:50] Tomás Rivera:
    Okay. If the rate holds, my list is: clear the Reno backlog, launch
    the address-validation prompt, and start the weekend-coverage pilot.
    If we lose budget, we drop the weekend pilot and keep address
    validation as minimum-viable scope. If we lose more than that, the
    prompt also slips and we go into a maintenance posture.

[15:03:40] Grace Okafor:
    I'd add: if we go into maintenance mode, we should aggressively cut
    manual review burden by retiring the legacy returns queue rather than
    trying to keep both queues alive. The two-week overlap is fine; an
    indefinite overlap will eat us.

[15:05:20] Daniel Brooks:
    Agreed. And on the Kestrel SKU timing — if Q3 is a cost-cut quarter,
    do I push the buy-box demotion to Q4? It feels weird to demote KSO-
    8842 in a quarter where we're also asking Kestrel for inbound
    priority.

[15:06:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Let's talk about that Thursday too. Short version: the demotion is
    about the 4.8% defect rate, not about the macro. If the defect case
    is strong it goes through regardless, but the optics of the timing
    matter. We'll figure it out.

[15:08:00] Grace Okafor:
    What about the Swiftline-specific promises? If they raise rates, do
    we still honor the two-day badges on the affected lanes?

[15:08:40] Keisha Morgan:
    Likely yes for the current promo window. After that, we consolidate
    to realistic promises. I'll get clarity from Vendor Relations after
    May 12.

[15:11:00] Tomás Rivera:
    One more — the subscription-box insert redesign. If we're tight on
    budget, that's not happening, right?

[15:11:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Correct. That's a Q4-or-later conversation now.

[15:14:00] Daniel Brooks:
    Got it.

[15:18:30] Keisha Morgan:
    Good. Let me write all this up after we wrap and I'll share a
    fulfillment-planning doc just with the four of us tomorrow. AI
    notetaker will generate a summary of this whole review in a few
    minutes — I'll deal with that. Anything else for the good of the
    team?

[15:21:00] Tomás Rivera:
    Nothing from me.

[15:21:10] Grace Okafor:
    Good here.

[15:21:20] Daniel Brooks:
    All set. Talk Thursday.

[15:29:40] Keisha Morgan:
    Thanks team. See you tomorrow.

I'd like us to look at the cancellation list together instead of treating it as a churn number in isolation. Happy to talk it through whenever works.

Thanks!
— Jordan
